title: Wittmann wins the wet first race of the DTM turbo era
dek: Marco Wittmann won the first turbo-era DTM race at Hockenheim from pole in heavy rain, 13.727 seconds clear of Mike Rockenfeller, after René Rast's Audi stopped with gearbox trouble while running second.

chapters.title: A new rulebook and three makes on the grid
text: The 2019 DTM season opened at Hockenheim with a new rulebook and the start of the series’ turbo era. The V8s of earlier years had given way to two-litre, four-cylinder turbo engines of more than 600 horsepower, and the 18-car field was split between three makes: Audi, BMW and Aston Martin, whose Vantage DTM was run by R-Motorsport and made its race debut that weekend. Audi’s customer team WRT was also new to the DTM, with two cars, while Phoenix, a long-standing entrant, ran a pair of RS 5 turbos.

The sprint format meant one qualifying session and one race on Saturday and the same again on Sunday, with a mandatory pit stop for a tyre change in every race. Saturday was cold and wet, and drivers had to get Hankook’s wet tyre up to working temperature before they could use the new cars’ power; Sunday was forecast to be dry.

On the grid, René Rast arrived as the 2017 champion and the previous season’s runner-up for Audi, and Marco Wittmann as a two-time champion for BMW. Philipp Eng’s BMW, meanwhile, was hit by electrical trouble and managed very little running on Friday.

chapters.title: Wittmann finds the time on his final lap
text: Qualifying took place on a wet, cold Saturday morning and was stopped early, when Eng’s BMW coasted to a halt at the pit exit and had to be towed away. Eng never set a time. Once running resumed the drivers took more risks, and the times fell quickly as the session went on.

Wittmann took pole with a 1m48.215s on the last lap, the first pole of the turbo era. Mike Rockenfeller’s Phoenix Audi was 0.066 seconds slower and the pair were in a class of their own. Paul di Resta put the R-Motorsport Aston Martin third on the car’s first outing, 0.976 seconds off pole, which meant that drivers from all three makes filled the first three places. Wittmann called it a dream start after some problems over the winter.

Rast was fourth, 1.295 seconds off pole, in what he described as a messy session, with Robin Frijns fifth. Jake Dennis, in the second Aston Martin, was sixth on his DTM debut, and Sheldon van der Linde, another newcomer, seventh. Timo Glock, Joel Eriksson and Nico Müller completed the top ten, with Daniel Juncadella 11th. Loïc Duval, Jamie Green and Bruno Spengler followed, and WRT’s Pietro Fittipaldi and Jonathan Aberdein were 15th and 16th. Ferdinand Habsburg, in the fourth Aston Martin, was 17th and more than seven seconds off the pace, with Eng last on the grid.

chapters.title: Frijns jumps to second, Rast spins Glock
text: Heavy rain fell for the start. Wittmann got away cleanly from pole, while the cars on the inside of the grid found the surface much slipperier than those on the outside. Frijns used that to leap from fifth to second, with Rockenfeller dropping to third and di Resta falling from third to fifth.

At the first corner Rast ran into the back of Glock’s BMW and spun it. Glock rejoined at once but had lost a long way, and he spent the race climbing back. The stewards looked at the incident and handed out no penalty; Rast described it as a racing incident.

Frijns ran wide at the Spitzkehre hairpin within the first four laps, letting Rockenfeller into second, and Rockenfeller trimmed Wittmann’s lead to around a second. On lap 13 he allowed Rast an easy pass on the approach to the same hairpin, and Rast became Wittmann’s closest pursuer.

chapters.title: Rast closes up, then the gearbox fails
text: Rast, who had won each of the last six races of the previous season, got to within half a second of Wittmann at times over the next 15 laps, but he never found room for a proper move, and the BMW always seemed to have a little in hand.

Further back, R-Motorsport’s afternoon went two ways. Juncadella pitted on the opening lap, a gamble that gave him clear track for much of the race. Di Resta, who had run in the top five early on, slipped down the order and parked in the garage after 17 laps with brake trouble, and Habsburg’s car stopped after two laps. Duval had a brief excursion at the Sachskurve but kept his place. Aberdein had been running well until his stop, when WRT sent him out on slick tyres on a track that never dried enough, and the gamble dropped him to the tail of the field.
With around six laps left, Rast’s Audi slowed after the Sachskurve and he parked it on the grass with gearbox failure, ending the pursuit of Wittmann and the bid to extend his winning run.

chapters.title: A comfortable win and a first point for Aston Martin
text: With Rast gone, Wittmann made his mandatory stop a few laps from the flag and still came home unchallenged, 13.727 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller. Rockenfeller said his second stint on used wet tyres worked better than the fresh set had.

Glock, who had fought back after the spin, came out of his late stop as the net third, but Frijns, who had pitted a lap earlier and was up to speed, swept past him into Turn 2 while the BMW’s tyres were still cold. Frijns completed the podium 34.681 seconds behind Wittmann, with Glock fourth, 2.7 seconds further back, and Glock’s 1m42.469s on the final lap was the fastest of the race.

Duval was fifth and van der Linde sixth, the best of the debutants, ahead of Spengler and Müller. Juncadella’s ninth place brought Aston Martin its first points in the DTM, and Fittipaldi took the last point, tenth, for WRT. Dennis lost time with a problem at his pit stop and finished 11th, just over five seconds outside the points. Green, Eriksson, Eng and Aberdein finished a lap down.

facts.t: First win of the turbo era
facts.v: Marco Wittmann won the opening race of the 2019 DTM season at Hockenheim, the first race of the new turbo era.
